vsm2.14:131.0: The Formations Aggregate—See Tables II & IV
vsm2.14:131.1:
131. Now, it was said above, "Whatever has the characteristic of forming should be understood, all taken together,
as the formations aggregate" (§81). And here too, what is said to have the characteristic of forming
is that which has the characteristic of agglomerating.
vsm2.14:131.2: What is that? It is formations themselves,
vsm2.14:131.3: according as it is said, "They form the formed, bhikkhus, that is why they are called formations" (S III 87).
vsm2.14:132.1: 132. They have the characteristic of forming.
vsm2.14:132.4: Their proximate cause is the remaining three immaterial aggregates.
vsm2.14:132.5:
So according to characteristic, etc., they are singlefold. And according to kind they are threefold,
namely, (I) profitable, (II) unprofitable, and (III) indeterminate.
vsm2.14:132.6:
As regards these, when associated with profitable consciousness they are profitable, when associated with unprofitable
consciousness they are unprofitable, when associated with indeterminate consciousness they are indeterminate.
vsm2.14:133.1:
133. I. (1) Herein, firstly, those associated with the first sense-sphere profitable consciousness (1)
amount to thirty-six, that is to say, the constant ones, which are the twenty-seven given in the texts
as such, and the four "or-whatever-states," and also the five inconstant ones (cf. Dhs §1).
vsm2.14:133.2:
Herein, the twenty-seven given as such are these: (i) contact, (ii) volition, (iii) applied thought, (iv) sustained thought,
(v) happiness (interest), (vi) energy, (vii) life, (viii) concentration, (ix) faith, (x) mindfulness, (xi) conscience, (xii) shame,
(xiii) non-greed, (xiv) non-hate, (xv) non-delusion, (xvi) tranquillity of the mental body, (xvii) tranquillity of consciousness,
(xviii) lightness of the mental body, (xix) lightness of consciousness, (xx) malleability of the mental body, (xxi) malleability
of consciousness, (xxii) wieldiness of the mental body, (xxiii) wieldiness of consciousness, (xxiv) proficiency of the mental body,
(xxv) proficiency of consciousness, (xxvi) rectitude of the mental body, (xxvii) rectitude of consciousness.
vsm2.14:133.3:
The four 'or-whatever-states' are these: (xxviii) zeal (desire), (xxix) resolution,
(xxx) attention (bringing to mind), (xxxi) specific neutrality.
vsm2.14:133.4:
And the five inconstant are these: (xxxii) compassion, (xxxiii) gladness, (xxxiv) abstinence from bodily misconduct,
(xxxv) abstinence from verbal misconduct, (xxxvi) abstinence from wrong livelihood.
vsm2.14:133.5: These last arise sometimes but not always, and when they arise they do not do so together.
vsm2.14:134.1: 134. Herein, (i) it touches (phusati), thus it is contact (phassa).
vsm2.14:134.2: This has the characteristic of touching.
vsm2.14:134.3: Its function is the act of impingement.
vsm2.14:134.5: Its proximate cause is an objective field that has come into focus.
vsm2.14:134.6: As to its characteristic, although this is an immaterial state, it occurs with respect to an object as the act of touching too.
vsm2.14:134.7:
And as to its function, although it is not adherent on anyone side as eye-cum-visible-object and ear-cum-sound
are, yet it is what makes consciousness and the object impinge.
vsm2.14:134.8:
It is said to be manifested as concurrence because it has been described as its own action, namely,
the concurrence of the three (cf. M I 111), that is, eye, visible object, and eye-consciousness.
vsm2.14:134.9:
And it is said to have as its proximate cause an objective field that has come into focus because it arises automatically
through the appropriate conscious reaction and with a faculty when the objective field is presented.
vsm2.14:134.10: But it should be regarded as like a hideless cow (S II 99) because it is the habitat of feeling.
vsm2.14:135.1: 135. (ii) It wills (cetayati), thus it is volition (cetanā);
vsm2.14:135.3: Its characteristic is the state of willing.
vsm2.14:135.5: It is manifested as coordinating. It accomplishes its own and others' functions, as a senior pupil, a head carpenter, etc., do.
vsm2.14:135.6:
But it is evident when it occurs in the marshalling (driving) of associated
states in connection with urgent work, remembering, and so on.
vsm2.14:136.1:
136. (iii)–(v) What should be said about applied thought, sustained thought, and happiness has already
been said in the commentary on the first jhāna in the Description of the Earth Kasiṇa (IV.88–98).
vsm2.14:137.1: 137. (vi) Energy (viriya) is the state of one who is vigorous (vīra).
vsm2.14:137.3: Its function is to consolidate conascent states.
vsm2.14:137.5:
Because of the words: "Bestirred, he strives wisely" (A II 115), its proximate cause
is a sense of urgency; or its proximate cause is grounds for the initiation of energy.
vsm2.14:137.6: When rightly initiated, it should be regarded as the root of all attainments.
vsm2.14:138.1: 138. (vii) By its means they live, or it itself lives, or it is just mere living, thus it is life.
vsm2.14:138.2: But its characteristic, etc., should be understood in the way stated under material life (§59);
vsm2.14:138.3: for that is life of material things and this is life of immaterial things. This is the only difference here.
vsm2.14:139.1:
139. (viii) It puts (ādhiyati) consciousness evenly (samaṃ) on the object, or it puts it rightly (sammā) on it, or it
is just the mere collecting (samādhāna) of the mind, thus it is concentration (samādhi).
vsm2.14:139.2: Its characteristic is non-wandering, or its characteristic is non-distraction.
vsm2.14:139.3: Its function is to conglomerate conascent states as water does bath powder.
vsm2.14:139.5: Usually its proximate cause is bliss.
vsm2.14:139.6: It should be regarded as steadiness of the mind, like the steadiness of a lamp's flame when there is no draught.
vsm2.14:140.1:
140. (ix) By its means they have faith (saddahanti), or it itself is the having of faith, or it
is just the act of having faith (saddahana), thus it is faith (saddhā).
vsm2.14:140.2: Its characteristic is having faith, or its characteristic is trusting.
vsm2.14:140.3:
Its function is to clarify, like a water-clearing gem, or its function is to enter into, like
the setting out across a flood (cf. Sn 184).
vsm2.14:140.4: It is manifested as non-fogginess, or it is manifested as resolution.
vsm2.14:140.5:
Its proximate cause is something to have faith in, or its proximate cause is the things beginning with hearing
the Good Dhamma (saddhamma) that constitute the factors of stream-entry.
vsm2.14:140.6: It should be regarded as a hand because it takes hold of profitable things, as wealth (Sn 182), and as seed (Sn 77).
vsm2.14:141.1:
141. (x) By its means they remember (saranti), or it itself remembers, or it is just
mere remembering (saraṇa), thus it is mindfulness (sati).
vsm2.14:141.2: It has the characteristic of not wobbling.
vsm2.14:141.3: Its function is not to forget.
vsm2.14:141.4: It is manifested as guarding, or it is manifested as the state of confronting an objective field.
vsm2.14:141.5:
Its proximate cause is strong perception, or its proximate cause is the foundations of mindfulness
concerned with the body, and so on (see MN 10).
vsm2.14:141.6:
It should be regarded, however, as like a pillar because it is firmly founded, or as like
a door-keeper because it guards the eye-door, and so on.
vsm2.14:142.1:
142. (xi)–(xii) It has conscientious scruples (hiriyati) about bodily misconduct, etc.,
thus it is conscience (hiri). This is a term for modesty.
vsm2.14:142.2: It is ashamed (ottappati) of those same things, thus it is shame (ottappa). This is a term for anxiety about evil.
vsm2.14:142.3: Herein, conscience has the characteristic of disgust at evil, while shame has the characteristic of dread of it.
vsm2.14:142.4:
Conscience has the function of not doing evil and that in the mode of modesty,
while shame has the function of not doing it and that in the mode of dread.
vsm2.14:142.5:
They are manifested as shrinking from evil in the way already stated. Their proximate
causes are self-respect and respect of others respectively.
vsm2.14:142.6:
A man rejects evil through conscience out of respect for himself, as the daughter of a good family does;
he rejects evil through shame out of respect for another, as a courtesan does.
vsm2.14:142.7: But these two states should be regarded as the guardians of the world (see A I 51).
vsm2.14:143.1:
143. (xiii)–(xv) By its means they are not greedy (na lubbhanti), or it itself is not greedy, or it
is just the mere not being greedy (alubbhana), thus it is non-greed (alobha).
vsm2.14:143.2:
The same method applies to non-hate (adosa) and non-delusion (amoha) na dussanti,
adussana = adosa, and na muyhanti, amuyhana = amoha (see §§171,161).
vsm2.14:143.3:
Of these, non-greed has the characteristic of the mind's lack of desire for an object, or it
has the characteristic of non-adherence, like a water drop on a lotus leaf.
vsm2.14:143.4: Its function is not to lay hold, like a liberated bhikkhu.
vsm2.14:143.5: It is manifested as a state of not treating as a shelter, like that of a man who has fallen into filth.
vsm2.14:143.6: Non-hate has the characteristic of lack of savagery, or the characteristic of non-opposing, like a gentle friend.
vsm2.14:143.7: Its function is to remove annoyance, or its function is to remove fever, as sandalwood does.
vsm2.14:143.8: It is manifested as agreeableness, like the full moon.
vsm2.14:143.9:
Non-delusion has the characteristic of penetrating things according to their individual essences, or it
has the characteristic of sure penetration, like the penetration of an arrow shot by a skilful archer.
vsm2.14:143.10: Its function is to illuminate the objective field, like a lamp.
vsm2.14:143.11: It is manifested as non-bewilderment, like a guide in a forest.
vsm2.14:143.12: The three should be regarded as the roots of all that is profitable.
vsm2.14:144.1: 144. (xvi)–(xvii) The tranquillizing of the body is tranquillity of the body.
vsm2.14:144.2: The tranquillizing of consciousness is tranquillity of consciousness.
vsm2.14:144.3: And here body means the three mental aggregates, feeling, perception and formations (see Dhs 40).
vsm2.14:144.4:
But both tranquillity of that body and of consciousness have, together,
the characteristic of quieting disturbance of that body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:144.5: Their function is to crush disturbance of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:144.6: They are manifested as inactivity and coolness of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:144.7: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:144.8:
They should be regarded as opposed to the defilements of agitation, etc.,
which cause unpeacefulness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.1: 145. (xviii)–(xix) The light (quick) state of the mental body is lightness of the body.
vsm2.14:145.2: The light (quick) state of consciousness is lightness of consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.3: They have the characteristic of quieting heaviness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.4: Their function is to crush heaviness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.5: They are manifested as non-sluggishness of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.6: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:145.7:
They should be regarded as opposed to the defilements of stiffness and torpor,
which cause heaviness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:146.1: 146. (xx)–(xxi) The malleable state of the mental body is malleability of body.
vsm2.14:146.2: The malleable state of consciousness is malleability of consciousness.
vsm2.14:146.3: They have the characteristic of quieting rigidity in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:146.4: Their function is to crush stiffening in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:146.6: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:146.7:
They should be regarded as opposed to the defilements of views, conceit (pride), etc.,
which cause stiffening of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.1: 147. (xxii)–(xxiii) The wieldy state of the mental body is wieldiness of body.
vsm2.14:147.2: The wieldy state of consciousness is wieldiness of consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.3: They have the characteristic of quieting unwieldiness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.4: Their function is to crush unwieldiness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.5: They are manifested as success in making something an object of the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.6: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:147.7:
As bringing trust in things that should be trusted in and as bringing susceptibility of application to beneficial
acts, like the refining of gold, they should be regarded as opposed to the remaining hindrances,
etc., that cause unwieldiness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:148.1: 148. (xxiv)–(xxv) The proficient state of the mental body is proficiency of body.
vsm2.14:148.2: The proficient state of consciousness is proficiency of consciousness.
vsm2.14:148.3: They have the characteristic of healthiness of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:148.4: Their function is to crush unhealthiness of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:148.5: They are manifested as absence of disability.
vsm2.14:148.6: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:148.7: They should be regarded as opposed to faithlessness, etc., which cause unhealthiness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:149.1: 149. (xxvi)–(xxvii) The straight state of the mental body is rectitude of body.
vsm2.14:149.2: The straight state of consciousness is rectitude of consciousness.
vsm2.14:149.3: They have the characteristic of uprightness of the mental body and of consciousness.
vsm2.14:149.4: Their function is to crush tortuousness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:149.6: Their proximate cause is the mental body and consciousness.
vsm2.14:149.7: They should be regarded as opposed to deceit, fraud, etc., which cause tortuousness in the mental body and in consciousness.
vsm2.14:150.1: 150. (xxviii) Zeal (desire) is a term for desire to act.
vsm2.14:150.2: So that zeal has the characteristic of desire to act.
vsm2.14:150.3: Its function is scanning for an object.
vsm2.14:150.4: It is manifested as need for an object.
vsm2.14:150.5: That same object is its proximate cause.
vsm2.14:150.6: It should be regarded as the extending of the mental hand in the apprehending of an object.
vsm2.14:151.1: 151. (xxix) The act of resolving is resolution.
vsm2.14:151.2: It has the characteristic of conviction.
vsm2.14:151.3: Its function is not to grope.
vsm2.14:151.5: Its proximate cause is a thing to be convinced about.
vsm2.14:151.6: It should be regarded as like a boundary-post owing to its immovableness with respect to the object.
vsm2.14:152.1: 152. (xxx) It is the maker of what is to be made,
vsm2.14:152.2: it is the maker in the mind (manamhi kāro), thus it is attention (bringing-to-mind—manasi-kāra).
vsm2.14:152.3: It makes the mind different from the previous life-continuum mind, thus it is attention.
vsm2.14:152.4:
It has three ways of doing this: as the controller of the object, as the controller of the cognitive
series, and as the controller of impulsions.
vsm2.14:152.5: Herein, the controller of the object is the maker in the mind, thus it is attention.
vsm2.14:152.6: That has the characteristic of conducting (sāraṇa).
vsm2.14:152.7: Its function is to yoke associated states to the object.
vsm2.14:152.8: It is manifested as confrontation with an object.
vsm2.14:152.9: Its proximate cause is an object.
vsm2.14:152.10:
It should be regarded as the conductor (sārathi) of associated states by controlling the object,
itself being included in the formations aggregate.
vsm2.14:152.11: Controller of the cognitive series is a term for five-door adverting (70).
vsm2.14:152.12: Controller of impulsions is a term for mind-door adverting (71).
vsm2.14:152.13: These last two are not included here.
